subject.title: Workboard: improve stacked-card readability and human-approval visibility

question: Should Workboard represent human-approval/action-required cards as a first-class UI concept, a configurable prominent-label rule, or leave this to existing blocked status and labels?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the durable product contract is not: the fix could be a UI-local affordance, metadata-driven behavior, or a new plugin config surface, and OpenClaw policy sets a high bar for new config/default behavior.

options.title: Add UI-local human-action signal
options.body: Use existing Workboard status, metadata, notes, or labels to surface an attention count or visual affordance without creating plugin config unless later proven necessary.

options.title: Add configurable prominent labels
options.body: Define a plugin-owned config contract for approval-needed label patterns, with docs and tests for the new user-visible config surface.

options.title: Keep labels and blocked status only
options.body: Document the existing blocked/status/filter workflow and defer first-class human-action UX until stronger demand appears.

recommendation.title: Add UI-local human-action signal
recommendation.body: Use existing Workboard status, metadata, notes, or labels to surface an attention count or visual affordance without creating plugin config unless later proven necessary.

likelyOwner.reason: The Workboard plugin and dashboard surface history makes this the strongest available owner for deciding the user-facing product contract.
